Global Partnerships & Alliances leader with 15+ years executing GTM and partner ecosystem strategies across NORAM, APAC and EMEA. 
Expert at forging C - Level alliances with AWS, Google Cloud and Tableau to commercialize AI/ML, cloud and data products - owned a $12M P&L and drove 92% ARR growth in 12 months, scaled partner‑sourced pipeline 2.5× to $12M (converting $4.6M into new ARR), built and scaled a 44‑person global GTM team, and supported an $128M capital raise to accelerate product commercialization and revenue growth.

My background in SaaS growth, demand generation, and strategic alliances spans over 15+ years, including key leadership roles at IBM, ORBIC, USEReady, and Damco Solutions. I've had the privilege of working with Fortune 500 clients and technology partners such as AWS, Tableau, and Google Cloud, helping them reshape digital ecosystems through data, design, and disruption.

Currently, my key focus areas include:
 🔹 Establishing company presence in the NORAM region (USA & Canada)

With each engagement, I aim to deliver results that are measurable, meaningful, and forward-looking-helping organizations not only embrace the future but lead it.

If you’re exploring how to scale your product, expand into new markets, or raise capital, let’s connect.

Salespeople don't hate CRMs.

Updating deal stages.
Filling mandatory fields.
Writing notes nobody reads.

That's time that could've been spent talking to customers.

And every minute spent on admin is one less minute spent selling.

Recently, I came across Positive noCRM, and what caught my attention wasn't a long list of features.

How do you post:


"You left me on my birthday."

"Why did you leave me?"

"I loved you so much."

after allegedly being involved in the very act that took someone's life?

What makes this story even more tragic is that it wasn't just about two individuals.

Two families were preparing for a wedding.

A future was being planned.

Dreams were being built.

And now one young man is dead, one family has lost a son, and multiple lives have been shattered.

If you love someone else, say it.

If you don't want to marry someone, say it.

If your family disagrees, fight for your choice.

Walk away.

Cancel the wedding.

Break the engagement.

People recover from heartbreak.

Families recover from disappointment.

But there is no recovery from taking a life.

The saddest part is that honesty, however painful, would have hurt far fewer people than the path that was allegedly chosen.

What are your thoughts?

Indian Startup News How One Wrong Title Became Everyone's Copy Paste Headline


I'm genuinely surprised how quickly misinformation spreads when it comes from a few large media houses like The Economic Times YourStory Media Startupro.in & moneycontrol.com

Kunal Shah is reportedly joining WhatsApp as Global Head of WhatsApp not Meta.

Not as Global CEO of WhatsApp not Meta 

There's a huge difference.

Yet somehow, a couple of publications like The Economic Times & Moneycontrol used "Global CEO" instead of "Global Head" and suddenly everyone else started repeating the same thing.

At this point, even Google seems confused.😅

Let's be clear:
- WhatsApp is owned by Meta.
- Meta's Global CEO is still Mark Zuckerberg.

The role being discussed is the operational leadership of WhatsApp, similar to how Will Cathcart previously led WhatsApp as its Head.

A "Global Head" leading a business unit is very different from being the CEO of the parent company.

This is exactly why fact-checking matters.

One outlet gets it wrong.

Ten others copy paste it.

A hundred creators repost it without doing any due diligence.

And before you know it, the internet has collectively decided a new "Global CEO" exists of WhatsApp.😭😂

P.S. This is a great reminder that not everything trending on Google or social media is necessarily accurate.

P.P.S. Sometimes the biggest viral story is simply a copy-paste error that nobody bothered to verify.

#WhatsApp #Meta #KunalShah #Media #FactChecking #SocialMedia #PostBySG

If someone arrives 20 minutes late because their bicycle got punctured, should they be allowed in?


If someone arrives 15 minutes late because their scooter ran out of fuel, should they be allowed in?

If someone arrives 10 minutes late because they had a flat tire, should they be allowed in?

If someone misses their bus, catches a train, and arrives an hour late, should they be allowed in?

If someone oversleeps because they forgot to set an alarm and reaches late, should they be allowed in?

Most of us would sympathize with these situations.

But would we change the rules for them?

Every exam, interview, flight, train, and competitive process has a reporting time for a reason.

The difficult part about rules is that they must apply equally to everyone.

If 10 minutes late is acceptable, why not 20?

If 20 is acceptable, why not 30?

If 30 is acceptable, why not an hour?

At some point, someone has to draw a line.

The real question isn't whether a particular reason is genuine.

The real question is whether it's fair to thousands of others who planned ahead, arrived on time, and followed the same rules.

What do you think?

Can we officially declare Bajaj Finserv the greatest stalker of the millennium?


I've never applied for this card.

I've never used this service.

I've never even made eye contact with this company.

Yet somehow, they keep messaging me like we're in a long-term committed relationship.

Every few days it's:

"Dear Customer..."

Customer?

Sir, we are strangers.

At this point, I'm convinced Bajaj Finserv knows more about me than some of my relatives.

One day they'll probably text:

"Good morning Sachin G. We noticed you skipped breakfast. EMI options available."

Another year of this and they'll start introducing me at family functions.

"This is our long-lost son. He hasn't activated his #BajajFinServ #InstaEMI card yet, but we're very proud of him."

The persistence is admirable though.

Most salespeople give up after 2 follow-ups.

Bajaj Finserv is prepared to cross generations.

My grandchildren will probably receive:

"Dear Customer, your grandfather's EMI Card is still pending activation."

Some relationships are simply forever.

#MondayMood #Relatable #IndianProblems #CorporateHumor #Adulting #WorkLife #Humor #PostBySG
